body:
### Summary

`MiniFiles` crashes with `E5108: ... ipairs(nil)` when deleting a file (`dd` followed by `=`) while an LSP client advertises `workspace.fileOperations.willDelete` (or `willRename`) with a **missing / null `filters`** array.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open `MiniFiles` next to a buffer served by an LSP that advertises `workspace.fileOperations.willDelete` without a `filters` array (observed with a TypeScript/JS language server sending `fileOperations.willDelete.filters: null`; any server matched by `get_clients({ method = 'workspace/willDeleteFiles' })` whose `filters` is not an array reproduces it).
2. Mark a file (`dd`) then synchronize (`=`).

### Cause

`mini/files.lua`, `H.lsp_fs_hook_client`:

```lua
local method = full_method:match('^workspace/(.+)Files$')
local filter_configs = client.server_capabilities.workspace.fileOperations[method].filters
local filters = {}
for _, fc in ipairs(filter_configs) do
```

`vim.lsp.get_clients({ method = 'workspace/willDeleteFiles' })` matches a client when `server_capabilities.workspace.fileOperations.willDelete` exists — regardless of whether the optional-looking `filters` field is present (some servers send `null`/omit it, e.g. a stale static capability). `filter_configs` is then `vim.NIL`/`nil` and `ipairs()` raises `E5108`.

### Suggested fix

Guard the lookup (empty filters already means "match all" — the file's own documented default for misbehaving servers, see the comment above the `ok = #filters == 0` line):

```lua
local filter_configs = vim.tbl_get(client.server_capabilities, 'workspace', 'fileOperations', method, 'filters') or {}
```

### Environment

- Neovim 0.12.x (also 0.10/0.11: the hook is only disabled on nvim-0.10)
- mini.nvim current `main` (`9ee72c2` still reproduces)
- mini.files `options.lsp_timeout` default (5000)

comment_data.body:
> `vim.lsp.get_clients({ method = 'workspace/willDeleteFiles' })` matches a client when `server_capabilities.workspace.fileOperations.willDelete` exists — regardless of whether the optional-looking `filters` field is present (some servers send `null`/omit it, e.g. a stale static capability). `filter_configs` is then `vim.NIL`/`nil` and `ipairs()` raises `E5108`.

If LSP server advertises that it supports `workspace.fileOperations.willDelete`, then it *must* supply [`fileOperationRegistrationOptions`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#fileOperationRegistrationOptions) to describe it. The specification describes that it *must* contain non-null `filters` field. If the server does not do that, it doesn't follow the LSP specification.

I don't think adjusting 'mini.files' for such servers makes sense, unless it is either a very common misbehave or there exists a simple and concise adjustment that *doesn't affect performance*. This doesn't look like either of those cases, so I am closing as not planned.

labels.description: The behavior is not planned to be implemented
labels.name: not-planned

title: mini.files: E5108 ipairs(nil) on delete/synchronize when a server sends willDelete with null filters
